chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far al-Kumandani narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran narrated from Asim ibn Hamid, from Muhammad ibn Qais, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him), who said:

Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, revealed to Adam (peace be upon him): 'O Adam, indeed I am gathering for you all goodness in four words: one for Me, one for you, one between Me and you, and one between you and the people. As for the one that is for Me: that you worship Me and do not associate anything with Me. And as for the one that is for you: that I reward you for your deed with that which you are most in need of. And as for the one between Me and you: that upon you is supplication and upon Me is response. And as for the one between you and the people: that you be pleased for the people with what you are pleased for yourself.'

key_terms.فَتَرْضَى لِلنَّاسِ مَا تَرْضَى لِنَفْسِ: That you be pleased for the people with what you are pleased for yourself

ai.seo_question: What are the four words in which Allah gathered all goodness for Adam?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith qudsi as a comprehensive blueprint for human perfection, structuring the spiritual life into vertical and horizontal dimensions. It uniquely categorizes divine worship, personal reward, the intimate dialogue of supplication, and social ethics as the four pillars of all goodness, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of creed (*Aqidah*) and conduct (*Akhlaq*). This framework underscores that true piety is not merely ritualistic but encompasses a holistic relationship with God, self, and community.
